name: Inventory Panel
description:
The bag, opened. inventory.slotted_bag owns what is carried and combat.equipment_slots what is worn, and until this existed the only way to change either was to walk over something better: gear equipped itself on pickup if it beat what was there, and a thing in the bag stayed in the bag. Every crawler since Rogue lets you open the bag, look at a thing, and choose — wear it, drink it, drop it.

This owns the panel and the choosing, not the consequences. Opened and closed by input.toggleInventory; a cell is chosen by input.inventorySelect and an action by input.inventoryAction. Each action is a REQUEST to the component that owns the verb: `equip` asks combat.equipment_slots (combat.equipRequested), `use` asks inventory.potion_belt (inventory.useRequested), `drop` removes one from inventory.core_inventory — the store the bag counts — and announces inventory.itemDropped at the player's tile for inventory.ground_items to lay. It publishes the rectangles of its cells and buttons so a host can turn a click into the input, exactly as presentation.battle_stage does, and says what a chosen thing is worth by asking the slots and the belt. Nothing is decided here that is not already somebody else's rule.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Cells across. Six by four is a bag you can read at a glance; a bag bigger than the grid scrolls nowhere and shows its first page, which is the honest answer until paging is asked for.

inputs.name: startOpen
inputs.description: Whether the panel is up when the build starts. Off: a bag you have not opened is not on the screen.

outputs.name: cells
outputs.description: The bag's kinds as {item, count, x, y, w, h, worn, gear, usable, selected}, in screen pixels, for a host's hit test.

outputs.name: buttons
outputs.description: The actions as {id, label, x, y, w, h, enabled}: equip, use, drop, close. A button that would be refused is disabled, not hidden.

provenance: The next thing the Big Picture named for the Dungeon Crawler after the battle feel pass (2026-09-11): an inventory panel you can open and act in. Searched first: ui.hud renders panels a brick publishes and owns no bag; inventory.slotted_bag and combat.equipment_slots own the truths this panel shows and nothing owned the choosing. Library-native, written against the studio's HUD slot system and the stage's published-rectangle convention.
